[RDSC.5a.1a] **A read changes nothing a later read can see (all backends).**
Every backend's aggregation read computes its value from stored state as of the
step's clock, over the window at the firing ([LSER.14.1]). The number of reads
is unfixed under any evaluation strategy, so a read must be idempotent:
otherwise the result would depend on how many rules reference the series and in
what order they were tested ([LSER.8.8]).

A read may evict: drop the samples that have left the window at the step's
clock. Every read at that clock or later excludes those samples anyway, because
the clock does not go back, so whether a read evicts first changes no answer. A
read must make no other change to the state: no lazy decay, sketch-buffer flush
or compaction. The per-backend notes — the signal backings [LSIG.2.5] — are
instances of this rule.
